title: Boyle rolls to third straight district volleyball title - The Advocate-Messenger
author: Mike Marsee
description: Winning a district championship is always something to celebrate. Winning one this way is also something to build on. Boyle County defeated Garrard County in convincing fashion Thursday to capture its…
content:
Boyle County players are joined by their teammates from the bench as they celebrate their victory Thursday over Garrard County for the 45th District championship. (Photo by Mike Marsee)
Winning a district championship is always something to celebrate. Winning one this way is also something to build on.
Boyle County defeated Garrard County in convincing fashion Thursday to capture its third consecutive 45th District championship and catapult itself into the regional tournament with a shot of confidence.
The Lady Rebels rolled to a 3-0 victory in the district tournament final at Lincoln County, winning the three sets 25-13, 25-20, 25-5 in their 36th consecutive win against a district opponent.
'This was probably one of our best matches that we have played, and if we play exactly like we did tonight, we will beat everyone in region,' Boyle senior Gracee Teague said.
Things weren't expected to be quite so easy in the 12th Region Tournament, which began Monday night at West Jessamine when Boyle faced Trinity Christian in a first-round match, but fellow senior Maya Smith said this victory definitely put the Lady Rebels in a good place going into the regional.
'We have a lot of confidence,' Smith said. 'We're going to support each other, and it's really going to help us as a team when we're all working together.'
Boyle (28-9) has won its last 12 matches against Garrard since a loss to the Lady Lions early in the 2022 season, its last loss to a 45th District team.
The Lady Rebels, who swept Danville 3-0 in the district semifinals, lost only two sets to district foes this season – they edged Garrard 3-2 on Sept. 23 – and they made sure this match wasn't close by dominating two of the three sets.
Garrard (12-18) got the first point of the match before Boyle scored 20 of the next 28 to put the first set out of reach.
The second set was closer, tied at 11-all before the Lady Rebels took control, but the third set was never in doubt after they took a 7-2 lead.
The Boyle players said their defense set the tone for the match.
'We did a lot of reading their hits very well, and we always stayed on our toes and moved our feet to the ball and got it right to the target so we could run our offense super fast and put it right back down at them,' Smith said.
Boyle coach Eric Kenoyer said good defense was the key to getting on a roll.
'It enabled us to transfer into a quick offense,' Kenoyer said. '(When) we started the night our passing wasn't great … and once our passing got on point our offense went.'
Kenoyer said he thought the nature of this win would help his team heading into the regional.
'It helps with our mental toughness,' he said. 'There's areas we need to improve, and what I really appreciate about our girls tonight was even though we weren't playing great at times, they were disciplined, they committed to each other and they trusted the training, and that's all going to help us for next week.'
The match drew a better-than-average crowd that included active student sections from each school and another Boyle cheering section made up of junior varsity, freshman, middle school and elementary players.
Teague said the players welcomed the additional noise from those cheering both for and against them.
'When they're pumping us up and they're having fun, too, it just encourages us. It just makes us a better team,' Teague said.
Boyle pushed itself for the postseason with a tough schedule and gained momentum along the way. The Lady Rebels have lost only three times since Sept. 7 and had a 14-match winning streak in September.
Garrard swept Kentucky School for the Deaf 3-0 and edged Danville Christian 3-2 to reach the district final.
Coach Samantha Torres said the Lady Lions had some work to do, particularly on defense, before they faced Southwestern in the first round of the regional Tuesday.
'We've got a lot of kinks to work out, just building a little bit more confidence going into that region tournament,' Torres said. 'Boyle's a good team, they're going to swing a lot and we've got to be able to pass those, and that's where we ended up struggling on defense.'

title: Winston Evans Pike, Sr., 88 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Winston Evans Pike, Sr., of White Lake, Michigan passed away on Tuesday, November 12, 2024 at 88 years of age. Loving father of Winston (Teresa) Pike, Jr., Bradley (Teri) Pike, Alan (Kyla) Pike and…
content:
Winston Evans Pike, Sr., of White Lake, Michigan passed away on Tuesday, November 12, 2024 at 88 years of age. Loving father of Winston (Teresa) Pike, Jr., Bradley (Teri) Pike, Alan (Kyla) Pike and Angel (Matthew) Herdus and Barbara (Dr. J. Byron, II) Wilfong. Proud grandfather of Joshua (Jamie) Pike, Daniel Pike, Mark (Becca) Pike, Jasmine Pike, Sophia Pike, Todd (Kylie) Edgell, Martina (Trevor) Wood, Kristin Pike, Dr. Macy (Dr. Thien-Nam) Pike To, Haden Pike, Ethan (Rebecca) Pike, Noah Pike, Jocelyn Clements, Sydney Herdus, Kelsey Herdus, Dr. John B. Wilfong, III and Anna Lynn Wilfong. Treasured great-grandfather of Hudson, Archer, Lennox, Stella, Ezekiel 'Zeke', Tirzah, Lucy, London, Camden, Solo, Cedar, Sage, Valor, and Luke. Sadly he is preceded in death by his son, Randall Pike, his wives, Anita, Carolyn and Lynda, along with siblings, Marilyn Nichols, Norman Pike and Vonda Thompson. Mr. Pike was born in Royal Oak, Michigan on May 7, 1936 to Frank and Stella Pike. He was an ordained minister with the Church of God (Anderson, IN). He spent most of his life as a minister and traveling evangelist. His early ministry was spent as the regional director for Youth for Christ. In addition to his life as a minister, he was also a published author and recording artist. He travelled for many years as soloist, song leader, and evangelist with the Ford Philpot Evangelistic Association. He will be remembered for preaching and singing the word of God throughout the country. He was on the board of directors of Camp Sychar in Mt. Vernon, Ohio for many years. Winston loved classic cars and was an avid NASCAR fan. He enjoyed traveling and spending time with his family. He will be very much missed by all.
Funeral services will were held at 12:00pm on Saturday, November 16, 2024 at Bethany Church, 1375 Hiller Road in Waterford, with Pastor Dennis Henderson officiating. The family received friends from 10:30am until the time of the service at noon. Graveside services will be 10:00 AM Friday, November 29, 2024 at Lancaster Cemetery in Lancaster, KY. There will be a memorial luncheon following the service at Independence Village of White Lake, 935 Union Lake Road, from 1:30pm to 3:00pm. Memorial Contributions may be made to: www.campsychar.org/finances. html or write to: CAMP SYCHAR P.O. Box 241326 Lyndhurst, OH. 44124. Spurlin Funeral Home of Lancaster entrusted with local arrangements. www. spurlinfuneralhomelancaster. com

title: Deangelo Durham, 38 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Deangelo Durham, 38, of Danville, passed away Friday, November 22, 2024 at Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center. He was born October 30, 1986 in Boyle County. Deangelo is survived by his wife,…
content: Deangelo Durham, 38, of Danville, passed away Friday, November 22, 2024 at Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center. He was born October 30, 1986 in Boyle County. Deangelo is survived by his wife, Whitney Coffey Durham. Deangelo was a graduate of Danville High School and currently worked for Danville Office Equipment. He worked for Cracker Barrel previously for many years. He loved UK Basketball and Football. Deangelo was a family man, always putting his family first. His upbeat personality and bright smile will be missed by so many. Also surviving is his mother, Ernestine 'Renee' Durham (Darren Lentz) of Danville; a daughter, Kyla Durham, a son, Kade Durham, both of Danville; sister and brother-in-law, Trevania and Derek Lynch of Danville; sister, Terri Harris of Lexington; niece, Rheanna Lynch, nephew, Raylan Lynch; mother-in-law, Cynthia Chandler (Michael) of Bowling Green and father-in-law, Ron Coffey (Sandy) of Eubank; sister-in-law, Jessica Coffey of Florida; two brother-in-laws, Eric Coffey of Stanford and Jacob Chandler of Oklahoma and many nieces and nephews, whom he dearly loved. He is preceded in death by his father, Joseph Harris. Funeral services are 11am Tuesday, November 26, 2024 at Indian Hills Christian Church with Pastor Jim Cooper officiating. Burial followed in Bellevue Cemetery. Visitation is from 4-8pm on Monday, November 25, 2024 at the church. Pallbearers are Billy Wheeler, Josh Bertram, Sam Martin, Ben Bright, Timothy Puckett, Derek Lynch, and Derrick Knight. Honorary pallbearers are his Softball Crew. Arrangements are entrusted to Preston Pruitt Spurlin Funeral Home. www.preston-pruitt.com

title: Shirley Chumbley, 86 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Shirley Chumbley, 86, of Danville, passed away peacefully in her sleep, on the morning of November 20, 2024. A tribute to Shirley Temple Chumbley reveals a life dedicated to her family, particularly…
content: Shirley Chumbley, 86, of Danville, passed away peacefully in her sleep, on the morning of November 20, 2024. A tribute to Shirley Temple Chumbley reveals a life dedicated to her family, particularly her children and grandchildren, who were the center of her universe. Her compassionate nature guided her professional journey in nursing, a field from which she ultimately retired after years of devoted service to the state. Shirley had a passion for exploring the world, with travels spanning from Florida to California. Shirley found joy in visiting casinos, a pastime she cherished as much as her beloved trips to Sanibel Island. She frequently visited Tennessee , where she humorously advised against indulging in the local fudge. Known for her candidness, she expressed her thoughts openly and without reservation. Despite facing significant challenges and pain throughout her life, she embraced these experiences with grace and resilience, embodying the spirit of a queen. Shirley is survived by her children, Aliece Chapman, Deborah Koenig, and Jerry Wilson; grandchildren, Jason Shoemaker, Michael Chapman, Cytina Sallee, Andrew King, Dongayla Dobson, Shannon Harris, Phillip Wilson, and Justin Wilson; great-grandchildren, Brittany Sallee, Makaylah, Elizabeth, Rook, Triton, Jaxon, Cierra, Ciena, Cirrena, Cilena, Vera, Althea, and Amelia; and a great-great grandchild, Arlo. Funeral services were held at Preston Pruitt Spurlin Funeral Home at 11am on Saturday, November 23, 2024. Visitation was from 10am-11am on Saturday. Burial followed in Bellevue Cemetery. In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions are preferred to New Hope Food Pantry in Danville. Preston Pruitt Spurlin Funeral Home has been entrusted with arrangements. www.preston-pruitt.com

title: Kerry Dallas Brogle, 65 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Kerry Dallas Brogle, 65, of Moreland went to his heavenly home on Thursday, November 21, 2024. Born in Lancaster on October 12, 1959, he was the son of W.C. Brogle and the late Ida Mae East Brogle.…
content: Kerry Dallas Brogle, 65, of Moreland went to his heavenly home on Thursday, November 21, 2024. Born in Lancaster on October 12, 1959, he was the son of W.C. Brogle and the late Ida Mae East Brogle. Kerry passed peacefully from this life to the next, doing what he did best- spreading joy and laughter everywhere he went. Always quick with a joke or to lend a helping hand, he was a beloved father, grandfather, son, brother, uncle, cousin, and friend. Kerry was employed by Norfolk Southern in Danville, KY, but his real passion was his cattle and his farming. He shared that passion with his children and grandchildren, who are eternally thankful for the time spent with him. He was always quick to share stories about and introduce his family to his work friends. Kerry made everyone feel like they were his favorite. He made every room brighter. He was selfless, a true friend, and good to his core. Kerry is survived by his father, W.C. Brogle; daughters: Bobi (R.D.) Middleton of Moreland and Shelby (Jacob) Elliott of Lancaster; sons: Michael (Corrie) Brogle of Danville, Tucker (Michelle) Brogle of Lancaster, and Will Brogle of Moreland; Becky Brogle, the mother of his children, who he loved dearly; sisters: Leticia (Calvin) Smith of Moreland, Annita (Jason) Witte of Moreland, twin sister, Terry (Tim) Crawford of Bryantsville, and Lona (Kenny) Merriman of Hustonville; and brother, Thomas (Jennifer) Brogle of Moreland. He also leaves behind 11 grandchildren who think he was the funniest, best Poppa in the world: Michael David Middleton, Caleb Middleton, Jude Middleton, Blythe Middleton, Atlas Elliott, Shelby Grace Brogle, Annabelle Brogle, Clara Brogle, Owen Brogle, August Elliott, and David Michael Brogle; and many nieces and nephews who remember him fondly as Koggy. Visitation is 4:00 PM- 9:00 PM Monday at New Hope Baptist Church. Funeral service will be Tuesday at 1:00 PM with Bro. Steve Meece officiating. Burial will follow in Hustonville Cemetery. Pallbearers will be Michael Brogle, Tucker Brogle, Will Brogle, R.D. Middleton, Jacob Elliott, Thomas Brogle, Michael David Middleton, Caleb Middleton, and Jude Middleton. Honorary pallbearers are beloved nephews and nieces. Guestbook is available at www.wlpruitt.com.

title: Business owners in Danville recommended to correct records - The Advocate-Messenger
author: joselylabarrere
description: The city of Danville is contacting local business owners to verify the accuracy and currentness of records for business licenses. All business license holders will receive postcards in the mail…
content:
The city of Danville is contacting local business owners to verify the accuracy and currentness of records for business licenses. All business license holders will receive postcards in the mail requesting updates and encouraging them to respond promptly.
The postcard says business owners should update their information at www.danvilleky.org/business. This can also be done by scanning the QR code on the postcard or by calling directly to the City of Danville Finance Department at 859-238-1200. Business owners must complete this update by February 15, 2025, in order to keep their business accounts active.
Get a head start
If you want to get a jump on the process, the online form is already up at www.danvilleky.org/business.
Contact information
Business owners with questions about the process or other business licensing and permitting matters can call the City of Danville Finance Department at 859-238-1200 or send an email to finance@danvilleky.gov. The City is working to keep its records current so that they can continue to be appropriately integrated with the local business community.
Important deadline
Business owners are urged to file their updates by February 15, 2025. Not complying can affect their business license status. For more information, see the postcard that was mailed or the city's website.

title: Elizabeth "Daphine" Cox, 86 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Elizabeth 'Daphine' Cox, 86, of Danville, passed away December 14, 2024 at Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center, after a 20-year battle with Parkinson's Disease. From the beginning of her life to…
content:
Published 4:23 pm Friday, December 20, 2024
Elizabeth 'Daphine' Cox, 86, of Danville, passed away December 14, 2024 at Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center, after a 20-year battle with Parkinson's Disease. From the beginning of her life to the end, she was a warrior in every sense of the word. Her foundations were faith, family, and education, and she pursued each with determination, grace, and ease. She had a remarkable ability to be tough-as-nails and compassionate at the same time, and her guiding hand in all things was incredible to behold. A former schoolteacher, she also raised 4 kids and managed a 30+ year veterinary practice with her crazy but super-loving husband, all the while showing the way with toughness, joy, and compassion. Her success in life is evident in her faith and the spiritual strength of her family. Daphine was born on October 11, 1938 in Borger, Texas to the late William and Myrtie Hatcher. She is survived by her husband of 63 years, Dr. Melvin 'Doug' Cox; a son, Travis Cox (Julie) of Danville; two daughters, Tracey Delene Gaslin (Todd) of Louisville and Leslie Teryl Snow (Dave) of Nicholasville; son-in-law, Andrew Bennett of Seattle, Washington; seven grandchildren, Malcolm Douglas Cox (Caroline), Jenny Beth Penson (Tristan), Jackson Travis Cox, Shelby Faith Snow, Samuel David Snow, Allison Margaret Bennett and Zachary Matthew Bennett; and a nephew, Brian Jull (Krista) of Mills River, North Carolina. She is preceded in death by her parents, a beloved daughter, Tamara Lin Bennett, and sister, Mary Della Jull. Funeral services were held Friday, December 20, 2024 at Indian Hills Christian Church with Pastors Jim Cooper and Mike Crowe officiating. Burial was in Camp Nelson National Cemetery. Pallbearers will be Malcolm Cox, Jackson Cox, Samuel Snow, Zachary Bennett, Laddie Garrison, and Jim Powell. Honorary pallbearers will be Jenny Beth Penson, Shelby Faith Snow, Allison Margaret Bennett and Barnabas Sunday School Class at Indian Hills Christian Church. In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions are preferred to American Parkinson's Disease Association P.O. Box 61420, Staten Island, NY 10306 or visit www.apdaparkinson.org. www.preston-pruitt.com

title: William Cox, 75 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: William Cox, 75, of Forkland, Kentucky passed away at his home on December 15, 2024. He was born on June 27, 1949 and lived a life filled with love, family, and hard work. William was married to the…
content:
Published 3:13 pm Friday, December 20, 2024
William Cox, 75, of Forkland, Kentucky passed away at his home on December 15, 2024. He was born on June 27, 1949 and lived a life filled with love, family, and hard work. William was married to the love of his life, Janet Pevley Cox, for 56 wonderful years. Together, they built a legacy of love and devotion, raising two children: James Cox (Vickie) and Tina Reardon (Jeremy) and three sisters, Lavern Rice, Beulah Mae Rice, and Shirley Westerfield. He was a proud Papaw to eight grandchildren: Ashley (Cody) Phillips, Brittany (Chase) Broach, Casey Wilson, Dre' (Michelle) Cox, Devon (Brittney) Cox, Dylan West, Kimberly West, and Ashley Reardon. His family continued to grow, blessing him with fourteen cherished great-grandchildren: James Phillips, Creed Phillips, Martha-Faye Broach, Myles Carroll, Annzly Carroll, Lynnie Cox, Keeston Cox, Shaelyn Cox, Kyson Cox, Tristan Love, Konnar West, Darren Patterson, Kerrigan Patterson, and Issac Moore. William was a farmer and one of the finest mechanics in the community. His skills, wisdom, and work ethic were admired by all who knew him. He took great pride in his craft and loved helping others, always lending a hand to neighbors and friends in need. Above all, William was a devoted husband, father, grandfather, and great-grandfather whose family meant the world to him. He will be deeply missed by his loved ones and all who had the honor of knowing him. Private family services will be held. www.preston-pruitt.com

description: William 'Billy' Ray Manning, 75, of Stanford, passed away December 14, 2024 at Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center. He was born on December 10, 1949 to the late Walter and Lucille Preston…
content:
Published 3:12 pm Friday, December 20, 2024
William 'Billy' Ray Manning, 75, of Stanford, passed away December 14, 2024 at Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center. He was born on December 10, 1949 to the late Walter and Lucille Preston Manning. Billy worked in the maintenance department at KSD for over 27 years. Billy was a member of Worldstown Road Church of God. He loved to trade guns and knives but above all loved his family. Billy is survived by a son, Chad Manning (Dixie) of Casey County; two daughters, Chana Esparza of Danville and Jennifer Downs of Lancaster; three sisters, Barbara Manning of Springfield, IL, Patricia Poling of San Antonio, TX, and Margaret Peebles of Danville; a sister-in-law Barbara Manning of Junction City; grandchildren: Katie Franklin, Robyn Franklin, Robert Franklin II, Anastasia Blanton, Hannah Downs, and Christopher Manning; 18 great-grandchildren and special friend and mother of his children, Barbara Sue Whitfield of Casey County. Billy was preceded in death by two brothers, James and Richard Manning; son-in-law Dennis Downs; and a brother-in law Gordon Poling. Funeral services were held on Thursday, December 19, 2024 at Preston Pruitt Spurlin Funeral Home with Bro. Lonnie Goodin officiating. Burial followed at Hustonville Cemetery. Pallbearers were Robert Franklin II, Eric Wilson, Brandon Poff, Coty Wilson, James Davis, and Ty Naylor. Honorary pallbearers were Robyn Franklin, Katie Franklin, Daniel Leonard Jr., Dixie Manning, Anastasia Blanton, and Denise Downs. www.preston-pruitt.com

title: Carolyn Begley Bratton, 81 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Carolyn Begley Bratton, 81, of Lancaster, passed away Monday, December 23, 2024 at Baptist Health in Lexington. She was born on May 4, 1943 in Madison County, KY to the late William and Georgia…
content:
Published 1:10 pm Monday, December 30, 2024
Carolyn Begley Bratton, 81, of Lancaster, passed away Monday, December 23, 2024 at Baptist Health in Lexington. She was born on May 4, 1943 in Madison County, KY to the late William and Georgia Portwood Begley. Carolyn was a member of Grace Community Baptist Fellowship. Surviving is her loving husband, Harlan Dale Bratton of Lancaster; two daughters, Nancy Reynolds and Angela Dye (Dwayne) both of Lancaster; a brother, Michael Begley of Richmond; a half brother, Sonny Cole; a sister in law, Carolyn Hobbs; grandchildren, William Land, Wanda Land, Roland Land, David Dye, Chris Dye; great grandchildren, Kaleb Dye, Landon Dye, Aidan Dye, Kinley Dye, Kari Dye, Addi Dye, Kayley Amich, Hank Land, Loretta Land, Lindsey Land, Breanna Land. Along with her parents, she was predeceased by multiple brothers and sisters. Funeral service was 1:00 PM Monday, December 30, 2024 at Spurlin Funeral Home Chapel with Anthony Roy officiating. Visitation was 4:00 PM- 6:00 PM Sunday, December 29, 2024 at the funeral home. Burial will follow the funeral at Camp Nelson National Cemetery in Nicholasville, KY. Pallbearers are David Dye, Chris Dye, Aidan Dye, Landon Dye, Seth Smith, and Nathaniel Woolery.

title: Bruce Richardson inducted as the 2024 Arts Citizen of the Year - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Correction: The print edition of this article in the January 7 paper incorrectly listed that Mr. Richardson was deceased. That information is not correct. This was an error by the Advocate-Messenger…
content:
Correction: The print edition of this article in the January 7 paper incorrectly listed that Mr. Richardson was deceased. That information is not correct. This was an error by the Advocate-Messenger staff and not the Arts Council. The Advocate-Messenger deeply regrets this egregious error and will work in the future to ensure that it never happens again.
The Arts Commission of Danville/Boyle County will honor Bruce Richardson as the 2024 Arts Citizen of the Year at the Danville City Commission meeting held on January 13, 2025, at 5:30 p.m. The ceremony will be held in City Hall with a public reception afterward to celebrate Richardson's extraordinary contributions to the arts community.
Founded in 2004 the Arts Commission awards the Arts Citizen of the Year to individuals and organizations who have made an impact on their community's local arts scene. Past honorees have included musicians, visual artists, playwrights, and community leaders, along with special honors for organizations such as the Farmers Market and the Norton Center.
Richardson's work as a musician, teacher, writer, and community leader makes him an appropriate addition to this esteemed roster.
A respected leader in the world of music and his community
Bruce Richardson came to Danville from Versailles in 1984. From there he was Minister of Music at Lexington Avenue Baptist Church until 1995, where he built a full choral program, supervised the installation of a 32-rank Moller Pipe Organ, and produced major musical works, including Menotti's Amahl and the Night Visitors and Fauré's Requiem.
In 1990, he founded and directed the Danville Children's Choirs, which organized 50 gifted singers from five Central Kentucky counties. The choir sang at such prominent venues as Carnegie Hall, the University of Chicago, Disney World, and the St. Louis Cathedral in New Orleans.
Richardson has also championed the arts through leadership positions in local organizations. He served on the Arts Commission's first board of directors and later on the board of the Art Center of the Bluegrass. He has been president of the Brass Band Festival and the Perryville Preservation Association and served two terms as mayor of Perryville.
A polymath: Artist, writer and more
Besides music, Richardson is an artist and author. His photographic series Looking Deeply into Tea has been exhibited at various locations, including the Art Center of the Bluegrass and the Lexington Public Library. He has also written and photographed a dozen books, alongside countless magazine articles, solidifying his impact on the arts.
Richardson is also featured in the documentary TEA: The Drink That Changed the World, available to stream on Amazon Prime.
Looking ahead
Richardson continues to be active in the arts community, tutoring his grandsons in violin studies and conducting art history tours. In 2023, he co-led a Harvard tour to Boston for the Art Center of the Bluegrass, and he has co-taught Japanese art history classes at Centre College.
The Arts Commission invites the public to attend the Jan. 13 ceremony and reception honoring Richardson and his contributions to Danville at Danville City Hall. His lifelong commitment to the arts has helped shape the cultural landscape of the community and inspired countless generations to come.

title: Robert Murrel Spalding, 92 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Robert Murrel Spalding, 92, of Broomfield, Colorado (formerly of Danville) passed away January 8, 2025. He was born on April 22, 1932 in Cincinnati, Ohio to the late Wesley Spalding and Edna Bonta…
content:
Published 11:13 am Monday, January 13, 2025
Robert Murrel Spalding, 92, of Broomfield, Colorado (formerly of Danville) passed away January 8, 2025. He was born on April 22, 1932 in Cincinnati, Ohio to the late Wesley Spalding and Edna Bonta Spalding. He is survived by his loving wife Mary Catherine Spalding whom he married on April 9, 1955. Robert was an Operations Engineer at Continental Can Company, Formica Corporation, and Bueno Foods Corporation, and was a Commercial Pilot. He served his country as a Captain in the US Air Force and was a member of the Presbyterian Church of Danville. Robert received his BA in Political Science at the University of Cincinnati in 1954 and his MBA at Xavier University in 1964. He is survived by a daughter, Cathleen Spalding Burns (Jack) of Erie, CO; a son, Matthew Spalding of Cornelius, NC; four grandchildren, Bryan Burns (Megan Canon), Caitlin Burns Bump (Stephen) Carynne Spalding Jarrell (Michael), and Katherine Spalding (Brian Booe); and four great grandchildren, Kelsey Faith Bump, Jackson Robert Bump, Lucas Canon Burns, and Riley Daniel Jarrell. In addition to his parents, Robert was preceded in death by a son, Robert M. Spalding, Jr.
Funeral services will be held at 12 PM on Saturday, January 18, 2024 at Preston Pruitt Spurlin Funeral Home Chapel with Pastor Sean Gladding officiating with burial to follow at Old Liberty Cemetery in Marion County. Visitation will be Saturday January 18, 2024 from 11 AM until the time of the funeral at the funeral home.

title: Roger Dale O'Hair Sr., 75 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: We regret to announce the passing of Roger Dale O'Hair Sr., age 75, who passed away peacefully on January 6th, 2025 in Danville, Kentucky. Roger Dale O'Hair Sr. was the business owner of Triple O…
content:
Published 8:59 am Monday, January 13, 2025
We regret to announce the passing of Roger Dale O'Hair Sr., age 75, who passed away peacefully on January 6th, 2025 in Danville, Kentucky.
Roger Dale O'Hair Sr. was the business owner of Triple O Electric for over 30 years. He was a respected member of his profession known for his dedication and passion. Roger had an impact on individuals everywhere he went. He will truly be missed by many. Roger was born on August 13th, 1949. He resided in Wolfe and Menifee counties until he moved to Danville, Ky. Roger Dale O'Hair Sr. is proceeded in death by his parents, Jack & Daisy O'Hair, and siblings, Willie Buck O'Hair, Virginia Donahue, & Ronnie O'Hair. Roger is survived by 2 sons, Dale (Bridgett) O'Hair & Darin (Rebecca) O'Hair, 2 grandsons, Nathan (Kim) O'Hair & Zachary (Melissa) O'Hair, 1 granddaughter, Olivia O'Hair, 2 sisters, India (Tony) Riddell & Gay (Harold) Worthy, and a host of family and friends. Services for Mr. O'Hair will be 11:00AM Wednesday, January 15, 2025 at Kerr Brothers Funeral Home on Harrodsburg Road. Burial will follow at Stamper Cemetery in Campton, KY. Visitation will be 5:00PM to 8:00PM Tuesday at the funeral home.

content:
Published 9:25 am Monday, January 20, 2025
Colby Young Warren, 27, from Wilmore, Kentucky passed away January 14, 2025 in Nicholasville, Kentucky. He was born on July 29, 1997 in Lexington, Kentucky to Wayne Warren and Stephanie Moulton. Colby was a resident of Jessamine County for most of his life, graduating from West Jessamine High School. Colby was a devoted father, always spending time with his son, often with his twin at his side from playing baseball together to starting their business or arguing with Abbie over the Chiefs. He was a family man through and through and will be missed by family and friends alike. He was loved. Colby is survived by his fiancé, Shelby Lindsay, son, Oliver Young Warren, father, Wayne Warren, mother, Stephanie Moulton (Woody), his grandfathers: Wayne Warren, Sr., Lawrence Deaton, and grandmother, Joann Deaton. He is also survived by siblings, Blake Warren, Lillian Moulton, Abigail Moulton, Maddie Isaacs, and Savannah Wilson; brother in law, Jacob Lindsay; niece, Chloe Lindsay; nephew, Wyatt Warren, extended family, Nancy Lindsay, Jon Lindsay and Carol Holbrook and his beloved dog Buck. He was preceded in death by his grandmother, Roberta Warren. Funeral services were 10:00 am on Friday, January 17, 2025 at Spurlin Funeral Home with Tyler Starbuck officiating.Burial followed at Wilmore Cemetery in Wilmore, Kentucky. Pallbearers were Blake Warren, Zack Bowman, Kenneth Luttrell, Hayden Smith, Daulton Osborne, Matt Vissing. Honorary pallbearer was Blake Smitson. www.spurlinfuneralhomelancaster.com

content:
Published 9:24 am Monday, January 20, 2025
Janice Yocum, 74, of Lancaster, KY passed away Saturday, January 11, 2025 at Ephriam McDowell Regional Medical Center in Danville. She was born in Plainfield, Indiana on March 31, 1950, to the late Balis and Lorene Stewart McKinney. Janice is survived by her loving and devoted husband, Billy Joe Yocum. Janice was a seamstress and avid animal lover. She loved her family with all her heart. She was a member of White Lick Baptist Church. Janice is also survived by two daughters: Scarlet Murphy (Steven) of Lancaster, and Christy Brutcher (Brad) of Louisville; one stepdaughter, Billie Dawn Harrison of Lancaster; a step sister Stacy York Isaacs; four precious grandsons whom she thought hung the moon; Tyler Murphy (Shelley), Seth Murphy (Paige), Peyton Smith, and Tanner Smith; and one great-grandchild, Eli Murphy; her beloved little dogs, Lil Bit and Jack. Funeral service was at 3:00 PM on Saturday, January 18, 2025 at Spurlin Funeral Home. Visitation was 1:00 PM until the time of service on Saturday. Spurlin Funeral Home entrusted with arrangements. www.spurlinfuneralhomelancaster.com

title: John Lester Wells, Sr., 85 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: John Lester Wells, Sr., 85, passed away on Wednesday, January 8, 2025, in Lake City, Florida, after a brief illness. He was born in Paint Lick, Kentucky, on July 8, 1939, to Cecil Wells, Sr. and Anna…
content:
Published 9:22 am Monday, January 20, 2025
John Lester Wells, Sr., 85, passed away on Wednesday, January 8, 2025, in Lake City, Florida, after a brief illness. He was born in Paint Lick, Kentucky, on July 8, 1939, to Cecil Wells, Sr. and Anna Mae Kinnaird Wells. Survivors include his son John Lester Wells, Jr. (Janet); granddaughter Jenna Wells, special person Nancy Helen Cromer and her son Jerry Cales, brother Harold Thomas Wells (Regina), sister Virginia Wells Fitzwater, and several nieces, nephews, and cousins. He was preceded in death by his parents, his brother Cecil (Bud) Wells, Jr., brother-in-law Oscar Fitzwater, and his former wife Carolyn Shearer Wells. John attended Paint Lick and Lancaster Schools and graduated from Trevecca High School in Nashville. He earned his AA degree at St. Petersburg Community College, BA and MA degrees at the University of South Florida, with post-graduate work at the University of Kentucky. He was a man of many talents and job opportunities: Grocery store manager, elementary school teacher, director of Maywoods Environmental Center, builder and landlord, and most recently, author of a book. He enjoyed fishing, hunting, telling stories, and spending the winters in his Florida cabin. Visitation was held on Sunday, January 19, 2025 from 1-3pm at Spurlin Funeral Home in Lancaster, Kentucky. Service followed at 3pm at the funeral home with Bro. Daryl Hodge officiating. Burial was at the Manse Cemetery (the Old Paint Lick Cemetery) in Paint Lick. Pallbearers were Rick Wells, Shon Wells, Jim Champ, Stephen Kinnaird, Allen Day and Wayne Day. Honorary bearers were Jerry Cales, Kurt Heatherton and David Kidroske. The family wishes to express their appreciation to Helen Cromer, Jerry Cales, David Kidroske, and Kurt and April Heatherton for their assistance with John's care. Suggested charities are: Hospice Care Plus, 350 Isaacs Lane, Richmond, KY 40475, or the Old Paint Lick Cemetery, Inc., a 501(c)(13) non-profit, P.O. Box 76, Paint Lick, KY 40464. Spurlin Funeral Home entrusted with arrangements. www.spurlinfuneralhomelancaster.com

title: Danville commission addresses petition to fire officer involved in controversial arrest - The Advocate-Messenger
author: joselylabarrere
description: josely.labarrere@bluegrassnewsmedia.com A controversial arrest and an online petition calling for the firing of a Danville police officer were the focus of Monday's Danville City Commission meeting.…
content:
josely.labarrere@bluegrassnewsmedia.com
A controversial arrest and an online petition calling for the firing of a Danville police officer were the focus of Monday's Danville City Commission meeting.
The incident centers around Officer T.J. Godbey, a former Stanford Police Department officer, and the arrest of 66-year-old Jon Hardwick at Walmart in October. Police alleged Hardwick was intoxicated and attempting to steal beer, but surveillance footage of the arrest showed a forceful takedown involving three officers. Last week, all charges against Hardwick were dropped, sparking public outcry and a petition that has gained thousands of signatures.
At the meeting, residents voiced concerns over Godbey's conduct and the dropped charges.
City leaders announced that both internal and external reviews of the incident are underway.
'We recognize that many folks are alarmed by the situation. These reviews will help us better understand the full context of this incident,' Mayor James Atkins said.
Danville Police Chief Tony Gray addressed the public, emphasizing the department's commitment to transparency and accountability.
'We recognize we serve with the consent of our citizens. I ask for your patience and trust as we move forward with this process,' Gray said.
The city commission has not made a final decision regarding Officer Godbey's employment.

title: Lora Jean (May) Thompson, 69 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Lora Jean (May) Thompson, 69, wife to Billy Thompson for 45 years, died peacefully at home on Friday January 31, 2025. She was born on July 22, 1955 in Lebanon, Kentucky, the daughter of the late Steve May and Marguerite Wade May. She was one of seven (7) children and six (6) daughters. She graduated […]
content:
Published 9:08 am Monday, February 3, 2025
Lora Jean (May) Thompson, 69, wife to Billy Thompson for 45 years, died peacefully at home on Friday January 31, 2025. She was born on July 22, 1955 in Lebanon, Kentucky, the daughter of the late Steve May and Marguerite Wade May. She was one of seven (7) children and six (6) daughters. She graduated from Marion County High School in 1973. She had a funny sense of humor, liked her dogs and enjoyed pie. She made good chili and, at Christmas, crunch cake. Lora found pleasure in reading and sewing. She owned and operated Pleasure of Pictures, a shop in Danville, Kentucky where she framed pictures and sewed curtains. Later, with her husband, she was the co-owner of Main Street Furniture of Danville. She raised her children in Danville where she will be remembered fondly by countless friends and neighbors.
She was a loving mother to Jason David Thompson (Lauren) of Lexington, Kentucky, and Nicholas Ryan Thompson (Ashley) of Lexington, Kentucky and grandmother to Jude and Finn Thompson. She was preceded in death by grandchildren Jalen and Kaden.
She is survived by her sisters, Brenda Followell (Billy), Genny Mattingly (Joe Allen), Barbara Rucker (Danny – deceased), Linda Crouch (Jackie), and Wanda Hennon (Gordon), and her brother, Jimmy May (Joyce); in-laws, Jackie (Joe Mark) Craig, Elaine Cecil (Jim Bean- deceased), Willard Thompson Jr. (Brenda Kay). She also leaves behind a large extended family including numerous nieces and nephews.
Funeral services will be held at 11:00 a.m. on Tuesday, February 4, 2025 at Bosley Funeral Home, 246 S. Proctor Knott Avenue, Lebanon, Kentucky, presided by Deacon Dennis May. Interment will follow in St. Charles Cemetery.
Visitation will be from 5:00-8:00 P.M. on Monday February 3, 2025 at Bosley Funeral Home, with a prayer service at 7:00 P.M. officiated by Deacon Dennis May.
Pallbearers are Jimmy May, Billy Followell, Joe Allen Mattingly, Jackie Crouch, Troy Rucker, Joe Mark Craig, Willard Thompson Jr., and Timmy Cecil.

title: William Lorenzo "Ren" Hankla, 78 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: William Lorenzo 'Ren' Hankla, 78, passed away peacefully on Monday, February 10, 2025, at his home in Perryville, Kentucky. Born and raised in Boyle County, Ren was a proud graduate of Danville High…
content:
Published 3:29 pm Monday, February 17, 2025
William Lorenzo 'Ren' Hankla, 78, passed away peacefully on Monday, February 10, 2025, at his home in Perryville, Kentucky. Born and raised in Boyle County, Ren was a proud graduate of Danville High School and the University of Kentucky. He served his country honorably as a Morse Code Interceptor in the U.S. Army's USAR Control Group, earning the Outstanding Trainee Award, the National Defense Service Medal, and recognition as an outstanding marksman. Ren was also honored with the title of Kentucky Colonel, the highest title of honor bestowed by the Commonwealth of Kentucky as well as a dedicated member of the Sons of the American Revolution.
Ren's career was marked by his roles as a business manager at Rough River State Park and as a sales representative for various farm equipment companies, including Star Line and Land Pride.
An avid water enthusiast, Ren found peace and happiness on the water. Whether skiing, surfing, scuba diving, or teaching others to ski and swim, his love for the lake was infectious. He took great pride in crafting the perfect tube ride and creating unforgettable memories for his loved ones. Also in his early years, he ventured into modeling through commercials and runway shows.
However, Ren's true passion was the Hankla family farm, which he proudly managed for 32 years as the seventh generation to own and operate the land. He found joy in maintaining the fields with his meticulously restored vintage tractors, exploring the woods, fishing in the Chaplin River, and hosting cherished week-long family reunions for 20 years. Committed to preserving the land's legacy, he protected it with a conservation easement and was amember of the Perryville Battlefield Preservation Association (PBPA), passionately working to protect and preserve the historical integrity of the Perryville Battlefield.
Above all, Ren's relationship with God was first and foremost in his life. His faith was the foundation of his character, guiding his every step and decision. He lived with humility, integrity, and compassion, always striving to reflect Christ's love in his actions and words. His unwavering faith provided comfort and strength throughout his life.
Ren is survived by his beloved wife of 49 years, Faye Gossett; daughters Renée Hankla of Salinas, CA, and Heather Lea of Nashville, TN; stepdaughter Carol Raskin (David) of Salvisa; stepson Kerry Robison (Marshele) of Greenville; five grandchildren—William Hankla, Marina Bernstein, Matthew and Kola Raskin, and Jes Robison; and his brother, Scott Hankla (Mary Pat) of Frankfort.
He was preceded in death by his parents, Henry Scott and Virginia Pettus Hankla; sister Martha Hankla McGee and brother David Bitzer.
Ren will be remembered for his deep faith, dedication to his family, and his unwavering commitment to preserving his family's legacy. His memory will live on in the hearts of all who knew and loved him.
A celebration of his life will be held on Sunday, February 23, 2025, at Perryville Community Church, with visitation beginning at 12:30 pm and the memorial service at 1:30 pm. Reverend Paul Moore and Doug Lester will officiate. Following the memorial service, Ren will be laid to rest with military honors at Hillcrest Cemetery in Perryville. Arrangements are under the care of Walden Funeral Home. In lieu of flowers, please send donations to Perryville Battlefield State Park, PO Box 296, Perryville, Ky. in memory of Ren Hankla.

title: Standing Firm: Kentucky must reject HB368 and SB218 to protect open government - The Advocate-Messenger
author: Staff Reports
description: As lawmakers in the Kentucky General Assembly review proposed legislation, two bills demand urgent scrutiny for their implications on transparency and accountability in our state government. House…
content:
As lawmakers in the Kentucky General Assembly review proposed legislation, two bills demand urgent scrutiny for their implications on transparency and accountability in our state government. House Bill 368 and Senate Bill 218 seeks to remove legal notices from newspapers and place them on government websites. Websites run by the government themselves. That is a recipe for disaster. These bills threaten to erode the foundational principles of open government, a cornerstone of democracy that empowers citizens and holds public officials accountable. At their core, HB368 and SB218 provide crucial guidelines for the publication of public notices, ensuring that vital information reaches the hands of citizens who have a right to know about government actions and decisions. They propose significant changes that could lead to reduced public access to important information regarding local and state government operations. This is a concerning direction. The importance of transparency in government cannot be overstated. A government that operates in secrecy is one that is unaccountable to its citizens. The proposed amendments could lead to fewer public notices being published in community papers, effectively diminishing the opportunity for citizens to engage with their government. It is essential that the citizens of Kentucky
remain informed about government decisions that may
affect their lives, from budget allocations to changes in local ordinances. Moreover, the move to limit the accessibility of public notices could disproportionately impact rural communities, including those without easy access to online resources. In rural areas where internet connectivity is often unreliable, traditional print media remains a lifeline for accessing essential information. Reducing the avenues for public engagement may further alienate these communities and hinder their ability to advocate for their rights and needs. Lawmakers must prioritize the voices of their constituents over bureaucratic convenience. A vote against HB368 and SB218 is a vote in favor of transparency, public engagement, and the protection of democratic principles. By rejecting this measure, Kentucky lawmakers can demonstrate their commitment to upholding the democratic values that define our Commonwealth. As engaged citizens, we must encourage our representatives to understand the ramifications of their votes on HB368 SB218. Let us remind them that an informed electorate is the bedrock of a healthy democracy. It is crucial that our lawmakers vote no on these bills to ensure that the people of Kentucky continue to have access to the information they need to hold their government
accountable.
In this pivotal moment, the choice is clear: let us stand together in unwavering support of an open and transparent government that serves all Kentuckians. Voting against HB368 and SB218 is not just a legislative decision; it is a commitment to our shared values of democracy, freedom, and public engagement. Call your state representative and state senator on the toll- free message line (1-800-372-7181) and tell them to vote
NO on HB 368 and SB218.
Joe Imel is the publisher of 8 Carpenter Media Group newspapers in Kentucky and State At-Large Kentucky
Press Association Board Member.

title: Chris W. Crain, 68 - The Advocate-Messenger
description: Chris Wilson Crain, 68, of Gravel Switch, died on February 25, 2025. Born on July 28, 1956, in Danville, Kentucky, to the late Warren Bruce and Glorianna Hourigan Crain. Chris was preceded in death by…
content:
Published 9:34 am Monday, March 3, 2025
Chris Wilson Crain, 68, of Gravel Switch, died on February 25, 2025. Born on July 28, 1956, in Danville, Kentucky, to the late Warren Bruce and Glorianna Hourigan Crain. Chris was preceded in death by his son William Crain, and his brothers Chad Ramey Crain Ray Ormsby. He joined the United States Army, serving overseas, and devoted his career to the telecommunications industry, where he served as a supervisor at TCI Cable. His commitment to his work and colleagues was admirable, and he was known for his strong work ethic and leadership skills. Friends and family will remember Chris for his strength, kindness, and gentle humor, brightening the lives of those around him. Chris is survived by his daughters Jessica F. Conder and Tammie Horne, his Step-Mom Barbara Crain, his brother Michael Bruce Crain; sisters Carol Michelle Hansen and Jacqueline Koch; grandchildren William Conder and Reana Harmon; great-grandchildren Nevaha King and Noah Cummins, aunts Darnell Davis and Jane Hourigan, along with his extended family. A memorial visitation will be held 1 – 3 p.m., Monday, March 3, 2025, at Stith Funeral Home, Danville.
Chris Wilson Crain will be dearly missed but will live on in the hearts of those who loved him. For condolences and to share memories please visit www.stithcares.com

title: Danville to construct sidewalk on Baughman Avenue
description: Increased traffic and concerns for pedestrian safety have revealed a great need for a sidewalk along Baughman Avenue in Danville. The cooperation of property owners (residents), utility providers, and…
content:
Photo by Leroy Evans on Unsplash Increased traffic and concerns for pedestrian safety have revealed a great need for a sidewalk along Baughman Avenue in Danville. The cooperation of property owners (residents), utility providers, and city leaders has been crucial to moving the project forward in recent years.
Due to the location of utilities, the Baughman Avenue Sidewalk will be located on the north side of the street from Hustonville Road to Alexander Drive. A mini-roundabout will be constructed at the Waveland Ave intersection, meant to eliminate serious crashes and slow traffic. Construction of the sidewalk is expected to begin in late 2024 or early 2025.
The estimated cost of the Baughman Avenue Sidewalk Project is $500,000. The City of Danville has pursued and been approved to receive a KYTC Transportation Alternatives Program Grant, which will reimburse approximately $400,000 of the total cost.
Please contact the City Engineer's office at 859-238-1200 with questions.

During a meeting of the Perryville City Council on May 9, the council swore in a new K9 unit for the Perryville Police Department after their previous K9 officer, Liberty, passed away after four years of service.
'The city feels a significant loss,' said Perryville Mayor Rob Kernodle. Officer Larry Nunes has our condolences. We appreciate her time and Officer Nunes' use of her to our city's benefit. She was a great benefit. I think it is significant for a town of our size to have a K9.'
Perryville's newest officer, Geo, was acquired from the same organization that provided Liberty, the Sector K9 Foundation.
Officer Larry Nunes was presented with a commemorative drawing of Liberty.
Late last month, a Perryville firefighter suffered a medical incident while fighting a structure fire. Perryville Fire Chief Nathan Stevens explained that the issue was not caused by the fire. He said that Perryville FD has begun having EMT volunteers at fires, who were there to catch the issue.
'It was an issue he had previously,' Stevens said. 'It was just caught there. Luckily, we caught it just in time and made him go to the hospital; it was that severe. I have to give women firefighters I have credit for catching it like they did. Luckily, we have personnel who do nothing but monitor our health during a large fire.'
In response to the incident, Perryville FD policy has added that EMTs can force a firefighter off duty if necessary. In addition, the fire department and council have begun looking into funding EMT classes for interested firefighters.
'You can never have enough EMTs. Not in today's world,' Stevens said.
In other news from the meeting, the council reappointed Anne Sleet to another term on the Danville-Boyle County Human Rights Commission.
'She is proud to serve on the committee and willing to continue to do so,' Kernodle said.

title: Four local athletes win at CKC track and field meet
author: Mike Marsee
description: Two defending state track and field champions won their events Friday at the Central Kentucky Conference Championships track and field meet. Germani Crosby of Lincoln County and Jordan Piazza of…
content:
Two defending state track and field champions won their events Friday at the Central Kentucky Conference Championships track and field meet.
Germani Crosby of Lincoln County and Jordan Piazza of Mercer County were among four individual winners from area schools in the CKC meet at West Jessamine Middle School that included most local teams and was the final tune-up for regional competition.
Crosby, the defending Class 2A champion in the girls shot put, won that event with a throw of 38 feet, 10 inches that was one inch off her top throw at last year's state meet. She also finished second in the discus.
Piazza, the defending Class 2A champion in the boys 110-meter hurdles, won that event in 15.32 seconds, about a quarter-second off his time at last year's state meet.
Emmanuel Dut of Danville Christian won the boys 400 dash in 50.08 seconds, and Andrew Sparks of Garrard County won the boys discus in 154-10.
J.D. Cooley of Boyle County finished second behind Dut in the 400 and Boyle relay teams claimed two second-place finishes to help the Boyle boys finish third in the team standings behind East Jessamine and Lafayette.
Mercer finished fourth in the boys team standings.
Boyle also led all local schools in the girls standings with a ninth-place finish. Kendra Christopher had the top result for the Boyle girls, placing second in the long jump.
